Speed’s Caribbean tour felt like one of the wildest IRL seasons ever put on the internet 15 stops in just over two weeks, turning the region into a live global stage. It was raw, chaotic, beautiful, unpredictable, and sometimes messy, but that’s what made it feel real. Speed and his team pushed through long travel days, massive crowds, health scares, backlash, and nonstop pressure, and still gave millions of viewers a version of the Caribbean that no polished tourism ad could ever capture. With Bahamas closing the chapter, it’s sad seeing this season end, but it also feels earned.

if you guy's don't know what is jab or you do. jab jab is a  traditional grenadian masquerade celebrated freedom, resistance, and African  heritage,  central  to island's  carnival festivities. Origins and historical  significance, jab jab trances  its roots to the era of slavery on Grenada,  where  enslaved African  on sugar plantations created  this masquerade as a  form of resistance and it self-expression during carnival, witch was originally reserved for  the white  ruling class  or plantation owners. the term "jab jab" comes from French creole word for"devil" {diable}, but it symbolizes the spirits of African  ancestors   rather than demonic  forces. by adopting the persona of the "devil", enslaved people mocked their oppressors, turning a  derogatory  label into a celebration or resilience and liberation.

For those who don’t know

A plane engine is the component of an aircraft responsible for generating the power required for flight. Without the engine, airplanes could not take off, climb, cruise, or land safely. There are different types of engines used in aviation, but most commercial airplanes use either turbofan or turboprop engines. These engines convert fuel into mechanical energy and thrust, allowing the aircraft to overcome gravity and air resistance.

The heart of a plane engine is its ability to move air and fuel efficiently. Air is pulled into the engine through the fan at the front. In a turbofan engine, some of this air bypasses the core of the engine to produce additional thrust, while the rest enters the core to go through compression and combustion. This bypass air also helps reduce engine noise.

Next, the compressor section increases the pressure of the air that enters the core. The compressor consists of several rows of spinning blades that squeeze the air, making it denser. Higher-pressure air improves the efficiency of combustion, allowing the engine to produce more power from the same amount of fuel.

The compressed air then enters the combustion chamber. Here, fuel is injected and ignited, creating a rapid expansion of hot gases. This explosion of energy pushes the gases backward, which generates thrust according to Newton’s third law of motion. The controlled release of this energy keeps the plane moving forward.

The hot gases pass through the turbine section. The turbine blades extract energy from the high-speed gases to spin the compressor and the fan at the front of the engine. This process creates a continuous cycle, keeping the engine running smoothly while generating thrust.

Modern jet engines are made from specialized materials to withstand extreme heat and pressure. Titanium and nickel alloys are commonly used because they are both strong and lightweight. These materials allow the engine to operate efficiently without adding excessive weight to the airplane.

Cooling systems are essential to prevent the engine from overheating. Airflow is carefully routed through internal passages to cool the turbine and other critical components. This ensures that even under high temperatures, the engine parts remain safe and functional.

Turboprop engines are another type used in aviation. Unlike turbofans, turboprops generate most of their thrust from a propeller driven by the engine. They are more fuel-efficient at lower speeds, which makes them ideal for regional flights or smaller aircraft. The propeller converts engine power into thrust while the exhaust gases provide some additional propulsion.

The design of a turboprop engine must handle torque and vibration carefully. Propeller blades exert forces that can cause stress on the engine and airframe. Engineers use dampers and reinforced materials to ensure long-term reliability and safety during operation.

Engine efficiency is measured by how well it converts fuel into thrust. Modern engines are highly efficient, using advanced aerodynamics and computer-controlled fuel systems to optimize performance. This efficiency reduces fuel consumption and lowers emissions, which is critical for commercial aviation.

Maintenance and monitoring are vital for safe operation. Sensors inside the engine continuously measure temperature, pressure, rotational speed, and vibrations. Airlines schedule regular inspections and overhauls to detect wear or damage before it becomes dangerous.

Noise reduction is another important aspect of engine design. The large fan in a turbofan engine and the bypass airflow help minimize sound, making commercial flights more comfortable for passengers and reducing environmental noise near airports.

Engines also have safety features like fire suppression systems, redundant systems, and automatic shutdown mechanisms. These prevent minor problems from turning into major failures during flight. Pilots can rely on multiple backup systems to keep the plane operating safely.

Over time, engine technology has evolved significantly. Early jet engines were less efficient and louder, but modern engines are quieter, more powerful, and more reliable. Innovations like composite fan blades and advanced turbines continue to improve performance and reduce environmental impact.

Overall, the plane engine is a marvel of engineering. It combines physics, materials science, thermodynamics, and aerodynamics to turn fuel into controlled motion. Every commercial flight depends on the precise operation of these engines, making them one of the most critical components of aviation

What you saw represents ordinary Algerians, with their amazing youth and their warm, smiling elders. Even though the stadium incident saddened all Algerians, it remains a small part of the Algerian audience that misunderstood him, and he in turn misunderstood Speed. As a French viewer who’s followed all your streams, I just want to share my honest thoughts. I was really disappointed by the France stream...I knew it would take place in Paris rather than elsewhere in the country, but even knowing that, I expected something more impactful. Paris is one of the most iconic and historically cities in the world, and yet what people will mostly remember from this stream is one football stadium and mid football amateurs... Even the food was not iconic. Maybe I had high expectations, but it felt like the stream didn’t even scratch the surface of what Paris has to offer

I really hope Speed gets the chance to discover more of France in the future. The country is incredibly diverse. Each region has its own culture, food, traditions, and mindset. Because of its geography and long history, traveling from one city to another can feel like visiting a completely different country. A tour of France could bring a unique experience every single day and help people realize that France is much more than just Paris and parisians.
There are passionate and welcoming french streamers / personalities in many regions who would be excited to help plan something amazing for you and your team and introduce their local culture. I truly hope that one day we will see streams from different parts of France that show what the country is really about.

For anyone deciding whether or not to watch the stream heres what I thought of his playthrough below, as a speed and last of us fan who was waiting for this stream. Im not a hater, I love speed and the last of us, this is just my thoughts for anyone who wanna decide to watch or not. Hes a great streamer, not the best lets player tho. (His red dead 2 stream was great tho, way better than kais imo). 

Obviously speed is crazy, and his irl streams are great, but ofc hes not the brighest person in the world by any means, like, at all. So his let's plays of story games won't be very immaculate or immersive for sure. But holy shit it astonishes me sometimes just HOW stupid and slow this guy can be. Sometimes I genuienly wonder how this guy got through life and makes more than 90% of people on earth. If your looking for a lighthearted and something you can put in the background playthrough, this is for you. However if you want a real, thorough lets play of someone who is really immeresed in the story, talks about it and takes their time, JackSepticEye (for the last of us 2) and Eralia (for the last of us 1) is the best bet.

At the first ~2 hours of the playthrough prepare for him to have the comprehension skills of a 5 year old, literally. He keeps on asking whats going on in the game even though shit just started, he doesnt loot, craft, or look around or anythingand seems kinda peed off ngl. But when they get to Bills in the game, he starts to enjoy it a little more and starts looting and crafting and stuff.

For the puzzles sections he takes quite a while on some of them, keeps going in circles and continously asks his chat for help.

For the cutscenes he actually does pretty funny & good with his reactions, especially those in the later sections of the game where he gets more immersed, he keeps track of most characters names and realises (most) plot points of the story, so its funny and memorable. Although he gets tired near the latter parts of the game cause he was up for so long. 

Although one thing he never does in the game is read any of the notes or letters in the environment, throughout the whole game, and the last of us is a very heavy environment storytelling game, meaning it has a lot of notes and letters around the environment and rewards exploration with lore. Which speed does not explore that much, and every letter he comes across he doesnt read. 
 
He plows through the game and environments pretty quickly and doesnt explore much, if at all. He does some optional dialouge options, but misses a lot, particularly the ice cream truck dialouge options with sam and henry and also some movie and environment dialouge options. 

Overall, this let's play is kinda what I expected given his personality, and thats alright. I think speeds personality with games shines best with more action adventure, sandbox and platformer games. Games like GTA and action games is where he shines best as its funny watching him play cause you can pretty much do anything and everything which fits in with his personality the best. Games like the last of us which is so heavily story oriented and character driven is more of a slow burn and requires patience, which speed doesnt have a lot of lmao. But all in all its lighthearted and nice to see someone else play the game for the first time.

If ofc, you want a more thorough playthrough of the game, talking about the environment, details and story, while also reading the notes and stuff. JackSepticEye is the best in my opinion, his playthough of the game (specifically the last of us part 2) is so good.

Mongolian throat singing, known as Khoomei, is a unique and ancient form of overtone singing practiced mainly in Mongolia and some regions of Central Asia. In this vocal art, a single singer produces two or more pitches at the same time by manipulating the resonance in the vocal tract. This creates a deep, drone-like sound combined with high, whistle-like harmonics.

Khoomei is closely connected to Mongolian nomadic culture and is often inspired by the natural sounds of the steppe, such as the wind, water, and animal calls. It is traditionally performed by men, though more women have begun to practice it in recent years. There are several styles of throat singing, including Sygyt, Kargyraa, and Khoomei itself, each with distinct tones and techniques.

Throat singing is more than just a musical expression; it reflects the harmony between humans and nature, a core element of Mongolian heritage. In 2010, UNESCO recognized Mongolian throat singing as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳🇲🇳

Thanks to Speed for showing the real China through his non-stop, long-hour livestreams. China is a massive country where every city has its own character. We've seen genuine, kind-hearted people like Master Liang, Uncle Goose, Chongqing's Trump lookalike, the Chongqing tour guide, Shaoxing's sweet girl – they represent most ordinary Chinese folks. But there are also businesses like Mango TV, who are all about quick profits and pushing ads with no real care for people. This is the real China that's still developing – with both good and bad sides.  

The streams also helped us understand Speed better – this 20-year-old American guy. Before, only a small group of Chinese young people knew him, and I personally thought he was just a funny and quirky internet personality. But after watching his China trip, most Chinese netizens agree with me: Speed actually has great qualities – he respects fans, stays polite, handles situations smartly, and him and his team have crazy energy. No wonder he's got so many fans worldwide!  

Hope Speed comes back to explore more Chinese cities like Xinjiang, Xi'an, Hangzhou, Yunnan, or even Northeast China in winter. Just one small tip: Make sure to arrange security in advance, and try not to have your schedule pre-planned by your team or officials. The best livestream moments come from random interactions with locals.

Fun fact: almost all police in China has no guns and no other weapons. They deescalate by helping and talking to the violent person who's in distress. And if that doesn't work they use a stick with a soft cushion bow to fixate the attacker and calm them down through talking. And you can ask police in China for any kind of help such as carrying groceries of elderlies or finding cheap high quality Hotels for foreigners and the police will call back-up just to help you. That's what happened to us when we were in China. One of the police even exchange phone numbers with our tour guide and called us the next day to ask if we were satisfied with the hotel he recommended. Another time a police gave us his undercover cop winter jacket as a gift (with the police signs removed). I'm telling this stories over and over again because I was so shocked to experience that Chinese police works for the simple people and not like in the West only for the rich and powerful and against the people.

Hey, friends, let me tell you, the most mind-blowing city in the world —— Chongqing! Just imagine a magical maze with 32 million people, looking like it jumped straight out of a cyberpunk video game! Yeah, this super city has more people than the entire population of Canada, yet it’s like a hidden gem in the southwest of China!
First off, the architecture here is just insane! Ancient stilt houses cling to cliffs, while modern skyscrapers pierce the clouds, and those huge red bridges stretch across the two rivers like dragons. The colors and scale are like someone turned a fantasy painter’s sketchbook into reality! The infrastructure is even more exaggerated — roads winding through the mountains, subways diving into tunnels, escalators climbing entire hillsides, and even Google Maps gives up on navigation!
The most amazing thing is that such a huge city is still off the tourist radar. Unlike Shanghai or Hong Kong, getting here isn’t easy. But trust me, the bumpy flights and winding mountain roads are totally worth it! Why? Let me break it down for you:
History: This place was a major trading hub 3,000 years ago, and you can still wander through the same alleyways that ancient emperors walked.
Food: It’s the birthplace of Chongqing hotpot! With its boiling beef tallow base and numbingly spicy Sichuan peppercorns, you’ll get a mix of pain and pleasure as you dip the freshest ingredients into the pot!
Nightlife（06:12:51）: At night, the Hongyadong area looks like a fairy-tale cliff palace, with neon lights dancing on the river. And the rooftop bars? The night views are simply amazing!
But what makes Chongqing truly unique is its “chaotic aesthetics.” Old teahouses sit next to luxury malls, and monkeys wander in the forests beside skyscrapers. You might just have taken a river crossing cable car, and after passing through a tunnel, you’re suddenly in a bookstore, and then in the blink of an eye, you’re in a bamboo forest. The city is like playing hide-and-seek with you, with surprises around every corner!
So, if you’re tired of cookie-cutter cities and want to experience an adventure that feels like crossing dimensions, Chongqing is definitely the top choice! Remember to wear good shoes, bring your curiosity, and pack some antacids —— because the hotpot is no joke!🚠🌶🏙

I guess there will be some unfriendly remarks in the comment section claiming that "this is a government-funded promotional event". In fact, it was the MCN team that hosted the event for the first two hours, and the local government was not aware of it. After Speed's MCN team planned the itinerary in a chaotic manner and did not even connect with Shaolin Temple, which led to the tragedy of the first two hours, angry Chinese netizens (Speed's fans) complained to the local Culture and Tourism Bureau (it is said that several phone numbers of the local Culture and Tourism Bureau were busy at the time). After that, the local scenic spot helped Speed ​​find a master. The local Culture and Tourism Bureau (Dengfeng Culture and Tourism) also confirmed to the media that a large number of people complained to the local government and then sent people to the scene to connect. So this is not a so-called government-supported "promotional event", but angry Speed ​​Chinese fans asked the government to find a master for Speed. Speaking of which, what happened today is also very funny. Under the angry complaints of Chinese netizens, the government was forced to intervene in Speed's itinerary at the risk of being framed by Western media as a "government-funded promotional event."

Nice, but, Here’s a simple muffin recipe:  

 Ingredients:  
- 2 cups (250g) all-purpose flour  
- 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar  
- 1/2 teaspoon salt  
- 1 tablespoon baking powder  
- 1/2 cup (120ml) milk  
- 1/2 cup (120ml) vegetable oil or melted butter  
- 2 large eggs  
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract  
- 1 cup (150g) chocolate chips or blueberries (optional)  

 Instructions: 
1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a muffin tin with paper liners or grease it lightly.  
2. Mix dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder.  
3. Mix wet ingredients: In another bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, oil (or butter), and vanilla extract until well combined.  
4. Combine: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and gently mix until just combined (do not overmix).  
5. Add extras: Fold in chocolate chips or blueberries if using.  
6. Fill muffin cups: Spoon the batter evenly into the muffin tin, filling each cup about 2/3 full.  
7. Bake for 18-22 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.  
8. Cool: Let the muffins cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack.  

Enjoy your homemade muffins!

helpful. But there is a lot more connection to Outlast 1 and everything can be explained! Walrider also had a hand in it. And the developers confirmed all of this because there is a public comic series (unfortunately only in English) that was published by the developers themselves. This is about two people at Murkoff who are there to shut down critical opinions. In the first issues you get some background information on the first game + DLC. Then there is a transition to Outlast 2. I won't give anything away here because I find the comics really exciting and they are very well done. So I can only strongly recommend that anyone who is interested read the series (it's not very long) and everything is available for free as a PDF (see link below). That actually answers most questions and everything makes sense.
That's why I always find it a bit of a shame when the story of Outlast 2 is portrayed as bad. I also think the story of the game itself is bad, but with everything around it I think it's pretty brilliant. In my opinion, Red Barrels made the mistake of making this game the main game. They should have somehow implemented the plot of the comics into a second game and made the current Outlast 2 into a sensitive DLC. Then everyone would probably have celebrated it (because the game could have been massively shortened as a DLC. I think it seems very stretched). But that's just my opinion, of course.
Outlast is one of my favorite universes, by the way, so I've read a lot about it and know it pretty well. If anyone has any questions about the game, I'll be happy to answer them :)

No wonder most of y'all believe outlast is just a game but it's more than a game. Its unsettling atmosphere and haunting storyline make it an unforgettable experience but what if I told you the game draws eerie parallels to real life events from decades ago? specifically, the controversial and clandestine CIA project known as MKUltra which took place during the 1950s and 60s. This program aimed to unlock the mysteries of the human mind, utilizing methods that ranged from psychedelic drug experimentation to sensory deprivation and psychological manipulation. Shockingly, many participants were unwitting subjects, coerced into the experiments without their knowledge or consent. The game’s depiction of the sinister Murkoff Corporation conducting grotesque experiments in a psychiatric asylum mirrors the moral ambiguity and ethical violations of MKUltra. In Outlast, Murkoff seeks to manipulate the human mind and push the boundaries of science, often at the expense of human dignity and life itself. The game’s fictional experiments resonate deeply with the historical chaos of MKUltra, where scientific progress overshadowed basic ethical considerations. Fast forward to this day, and another frontier of neuroscience emerges.... Elon Musk’s company, Neuralink. This innovative firm focuses on developing brain implant technologies designed to help individuals with paralysis or neurological disorders connect their brains to computers. While this work holds immense promise, it also raises profound ethical concerns. Neuralink’s mission.. to interface directly with the brain... bears an unsettling resemblance to the ambitions of MKUltra. The potential for misuse or unethical applications, whether intentional or accidental, cannot be ignored.

On a personal note, my connection to this story runs far deeper. I was one of the many unwitting participants in MKUltra. As a child I was subjected to a series of experiments designed to push the limits of human cognition. These experiments aimed to create individuals with enhanced mental capabilities... be it super soldiers, psychics, or other extreme ideals. Strapped to machines and subjected to experimental substances, I became a part of a larger, horrifying agenda. By some twist of fate, I managed to escape that life, but the scars.. both physical and psychological.... remain. Even now, the shadows of those experiences linger. Games like Outlast and advancements like Neuralink evoke a chilling deja vu. They serve as reminders of how easily humanity’s pursuit of progress can cross ethical boundaries, leaving destruction in its wake. The thin line between innovation and exploitation is one I have seen firsthand.

So whether you're exploring the world of Outlast or following breakthroughs in brain computer interface technology or making fun of it or having fun just remember sometimes the most terrifying stories aren’t fictional. They’re rooted in our own history... a history that’s not as far removed from the present as we might like to believe.

The origins batik fabric are traced to Java Indonesia, most particularly the island of Java, is where batik has reached its peak. Here, Chinese, Arab, Indian and European traders bought and sold textiles and batik is first specifically mentioned on a cargo bill in the mid-17th century. From around 1835, textile manufacturers in Holland started attempts to mechanise the production of batik using copper rollers and a resin resist. When the Javanese proved unwilling to buy this cloth, it made its way to West Africa, where it began a life and a tradition of its own, one which continues to this day as “waxprint”. 

In Java, textile merchants responded to the threat by finding a way to speed up the time consuming method of hand drawing the design. Wooden block printing was adapted to batik with the invention of copper stamps (or tjaps as they are known) to apply hot wax.

kaluga (Huso dauricus), also known as the river beluga, is a large predatory sturgeon found in the Amur River basin from Russia to China and near Hokkaido in Japan.[1] With a maximum size of at least 1,000 kg (2,205 lb) and 5.6 m (18 ft), the kaluga is one of the biggest of the sturgeon family. Like the slightly larger beluga, it spends part of its life in salt water. Unlike the beluga, this fish has five major rows of dermal scutes and feeds on salmon and other fish in the Amur with its nail-like teeth in its jaws. They have grey-green to black backs with a yellowish green-white underbelly.

The kaluga has been hunted to near extinction for its valuable roe. Despite constant anti-poaching patrols, poachers still continue to catch the fish. In Russia, illegally fishing for kaluga anywhere in the Amur River is a felony punishable by law. However, kalugas are known to have an aggressive nature, and instances of them toppling fishing boats and drowning fishermen have been reported, although no concrete evidence exists of them assaulting or hunting people.

Description
edit

A 3.7 m (12 ft)-long, 500 kg (1,100 lb), 70 year old Kaluga fish which stored around 4 million eggs
The Amur river is an important habitat for the Kaluga sturgeon.
The Amur river, an important habitat for the Kaluga sturgeon.
The kaluga sturgeon is a massive fish, also known as the "river beluga". It has a triangular head with several bony plates. Its body is an elongated fusiform body with five rows of bony scutes: dorsal with 10–16 beetles (the first is largest), two laterals (32–46 scutes), and two ventral (8–12 scutes) between rows of small bony scutes grains and rarely more large plate. Lateral scutes are smaller than the dorsal and ventral scutes. The mouth takes up the entire lower surface of the snout, it is lateral, crescent-shaped, and extremely large. Parts of the mouth can move to the side of the head. Under the snout and in front of the mouth there is a transverse row of four flattened laterally barbels. The inner two barbels are more anterior than the outer ones, but they are similar in length. The snout of the kaluga sturgeon is short and sharply pointed. It has very small eyes, located immediately behind its nostrils.
Habitat
edit
Kaluga sturgeon are semi-anadromous, spending some of its life in salt water but most of its life in freshwater.[5] Kalugas are one of the four species of sturgeons to exist in the Amur River. The Amur River is one of the largest rivers in East Asia and for part of its length forms the border between China and Russia. There are two populations of Kaluga that exist in this river. One group of Kalugas spawn in the main stem of the river, while others spawn downstream and work their way to the middle of the river. In the early life of a Kaluga, the offspring prefer to live in a clear habitat setting. They prefer the point of the river where there is an illuminated white bottom and open space for them to swim way above the bottom of the river. The Kaluga also prefers to avoid any cover from the river. Observations suggest that the Kaluga embryos might do this to avoid predators near the bottom of the river. The Kaluga sturgeon are currently endangered now because of human interaction. However, environmental factors such as warm water temperatures pose risk for fungus over free embryos and could be a cause of death also. The migration intensity of Kaluga is also a big factor in the life of a Kaluga. Water velocity in the stream has a great effect on the migration of the free embryos, meaning that the greater the force of the stream of water is the more likely the embryo migrates. Migration plays a big role in Kaluga's early life. The migration of baby Kaluga is considered a passive migration because the embryos have no control over where the river flow takes them. However, when grown the Kaluga constantly migrates back and forth between upstream and downstream. The generation length of the species is not less than 20 years, comparable to humans.
Life cycle
edit
Kaluga Sturgeon hatch in shallow gravel beds in the freshwater estuaries of the Amur River. Their parents play no role in their lives. They remain in the egg from 83 to 295 hours and hatch with a yolk sac that feeds them for up to 8 or 9 days. After that, the Kaluga sturgeon are forced to hunt. They hunt for tiny zooplankton, insects, and shrimp. They reach the sea with the help of the current and remain there until they are ready to breed, between the ages of 10 and 14.
Kaluga spends at least part of its life in salt water and returns to rivers to breed. The Kaluga Sturgeon spawns in lower reaches of the Amur River in strong-current habitats in the mainstream of the river on gravel or sandy-gravel bottom at water temperatures of 12–20 °C (54–68 °F) in depths of 2–3 m (7–10 ft). Spawning peaks from the end of May to July. Adults spawn many times during their life cycle. Spawning periodicity is 4–5 years in females and 3–4 years in males. Water temperature affects the onset of maturity of females. Females spawn a year earlier during warm years than they would during cold years. Females are only able to breed every four years. Their spawning season begins in May and ends in July. Adult Kaluga Sturgeons travel in small groups of between 3 and 20 individuals to the shallow gravel beds to spawn. Sometimes if the Kaluga Sturgeon is too large it may die from getting stuck in the shallow water. The Kaluga Sturgeon can hybridize with the Amur sturgeon.
Diet
edit

Feeding behavior
Adult Kaluga Sturgeon have enormous appetites. They eat pike, carp, herring, chum salmon, keta, and most other fish or shellfish that can fit into their mouths. A Kaluga Sturgeon can live up to 55 years.
Conservation
edit
There are a few reasons as to why exactly this species is declining. To begin with, they are being severely overfished. Ever since the 1900s, they have been poached at an alarming rate. After World War II, in 1948, 61 metric tons of Kaluga was caught, an unbelievable number for a species of their size.[6] They are extremely vulnerable to extinction by poaching because they have late sexual maturity, which only occurs after around 6 to 25 years of age. Sturgeon Caviar output, including the Kaluga, from 1957 to 2005, averaged about 117 tons per year. The animals are being hunted down for their unfertilized eggs because sturgeon roe is considered a delicacy to people all across the world. This market cuts down on the Kaluga population and only hastens the process of their extinction. Another reason for the endangerment is river pollution, especially near spawning grounds. This has led to deformed eggs and has caused defects in birth.[7][8][6] Hybrids between Japanese sturgeon (Acipenser schrenckii) and Kaluga have been produced in aquaculture and have found their way into the wild, where they are now frequently found and pose a threat to the native parental species.[1]
Population trends
edit
Data regarding the population trends of the Kaluga sturgeon is primarily based on various catch methods and efforts. The species has experienced a significant decline in catches since the late 19th century. Notably, China observed an 80% reduction in mature fish between 2008 and 2018. In the late 19th century, annual catches were around 500 tons, mainly in lower river sections, but by 1992, this had dropped to 92 tons. In 2012, the lower river's stock size was estimated at 7,100 tons. While no commercial fisheries currently target this species, it faces severe threats from illegal fishing, particularly in Russia. This combination of factors has led to an estimated decline of over 90% in just 90 years, equivalent to roughly three generations of the species.[1]
Protection
edit
The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) is an international agreement signed by 180 nations designed to ensure that international trade in animals and plants does not threaten their survival in the wild. The treaty was drafted in Washington, D.C. In 1973 and entered into force in 1975.[9] The Kaluga is protected by Appendix II of CITES,[2] which includes species that although currently not threatened with extinction, may become so without trade controls. Regulated trade is allowed provided that the exporting country issues a permit based on findings that the specimens were legally acquired, and the trade will not be detrimental to the survival of the species or its role in the ecosystem.[10]
In addition, national laws have been passed to protect the Kaluga sturgeon. Commercial sturgeon fishing was prohibited in the Soviet Union during the periods 1923–1930, 1958–1976 and from 1984 to the present (Vaisman and Fomenko 2007). The Kaluga sturgeon was listed in Appendix II of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) in 1998.[2]
